Analysis.object: Exercise addiction (EA) can also occur in regular exercisers, not just athletes, and is often linked with disordered eating (DE) when body image concerns and perfectionism are present. These factors interact in complex ways, meaning EA is not always pathological but can signal risk when combined with unhealthy eating attitudes and excessive performance pressure
The cross-sectional design prevents causal conclusions, and reliance on self-reports, a relatively small and female-biased sample, and heterogeneous sport types limit generalizability
Future research should use larger, more diverse samples and longitudinal designs, while exploring additional psychological variables and protective factors to better understand and prevent EA and DE

Population.object: 18 years of age and have an active lifestyle with regular physical activity (at least once a week, for a minimum of 30min)
